scenarios.setting: 一家国际远程公司的招聘顾问 Sarah 约你做 20 分钟电话初筛。这是你第一次全英文面试通话，她的问题不难，但节奏快，你要在短时间内把背景、动机、英语情况和期望都讲清楚。
scenarios.title: 电话初筛：第一次全英文通话

turns.en: Hi, is this Zavier? This is Sarah from Northwind. Thanks for making time — do you have about twenty minutes?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 嗨，是 Zavier 吗？我是 Northwind 的 Sarah。谢谢你抽时间，你有二十分钟左右吗？

turns.en: Yes, hi Sarah. Thanks for having me — I've been looking forward to this call.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先确认时间没问题，表达感谢，并说自己很期待这次通话。

turns.en: Great. Could you walk me through your background, briefly?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 好的。你能简单介绍一下你的背景吗？

turns.en: Sure. I'm a full-stack engineer with eight years of experience. Currently I'm a senior frontend engineer at a consumer lending company, where I lead work on an internal quality platform. Before that, I spent two years on a supply-chain SaaS at Meituan scale.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你用三句话讲清背景：八年经验；现在在消费金融公司做资深前端、负责内部质量平台；之前在美团量级的供应链 SaaS 做过两年。

turns.en: Nice, that's a strong fit on paper. So, why are you looking to move right now?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 不错，纸面上很匹配。那你现在为什么想换工作？

turns.en: Two reasons. I want to work fully remote with an international team, using English every day — that's where I want to grow. And in the long run, I'd like my work to reach users directly, not just internal systems.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给两个真诚的理由：想在全英文的国际团队全远程工作、这是你想成长的方向；长远看想做直接触达用户的产品。

turns.en: This role is fully remote and async-first. Honestly, how is your English for daily standups and written updates?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 这个岗位全远程、以异步为主。坦白说，你日常站会和书面汇报的英语怎么样？

turns.en: Written English is my strong suit — design docs, PR descriptions, async updates, no problem. Speaking is what I'm actively improving: I practice every day, and I can explain my technical decisions clearly, just not always elegantly.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你如实说：读写是强项（文档、PR、异步更新都没问题）；口语是正在提升的短板，每天都在练，技术决策能讲清楚，只是不总能讲得很漂亮。

turns.en: That's refreshingly honest. Last thing from me: what are your salary expectations for this role?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 这回答很坦诚。最后一个问题：你对这个岗位的薪资期望是多少？

turns.en: I'm still learning the full scope of the role, so I'd rather hear your band first, if that's okay. From my side, I'm in the ballpark of what senior remote roles pay, and the full package matters more to me than base alone.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你礼貌地把球踢回去：还没完全了解岗位范围，想先听听他们的薪资带；并表明你参考的是资深远程岗的行情，而且看重整体待遇而不只是底薪。

turns.en: Fair enough — the band for this level is competitive, I'll share details by email. Next step would be a call with the hiring manager next week. What does your availability look like?
turns.name: Sarah
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 可以，这个级别的薪资带很有竞争力，我邮件里发你细节。下一步是下周和招聘经理通话，你的时间怎么样？

turns.en: Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon, my time, works best for me. Please send the invite and I'll confirm right away. Thanks again, Sarah — looking forward to it.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给出两个具体时间段，答应收到邀请马上确认，最后致谢并表达期待。

scenarios.setting: 你已经通过了所有面试轮次，HR Daniel 正式给你发 offer 并约了电话谈细节。底薪比你期望的略低，你想在不得罪对方的前提下，争取签约奖金和更早的调薪评估。
scenarios.title: 谈薪资：offer 之后的协商

turns.en: Hi Zavier, great news — the team loved your interviews. We're excited to offer you the senior frontend role. Do you have a few minutes to talk through the package?
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 嗨 Zavier，好消息：团队非常满意你的面试。我们很高兴给你高级前端工程师的 offer。你有几分钟聊一下待遇细节吗？

turns.en: That's great news, thank you. I'm very excited about the team and the product — the interviews honestly made me want the role more.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先道谢，并真诚表达对团队和产品的兴趣——面试反而让你更想加入了。

turns.en: Glad to hear it. So the package: base salary, annual bonus target of ten percent, plus an equity grant vesting over four years. I'll send the full breakdown in writing today.
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 很高兴听到这个。待遇是这样的：底薪、目标 10% 的年终奖，外加分四年兑现的期权。我今天会把完整的明细书面发你。

turns.en: Thank you. Having it in writing will help me go through the numbers carefully tonight. Could I ask a couple of questions now?
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你感谢他会发书面明细，说今晚会仔细看数字，并先问能不能提几个问题。

turns.en: Of course, go ahead.
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 当然，请问。

turns.en: The base is a little on the lower side compared to my expectation, based on the market for senior remote roles and my current package. Is there any flexibility on the base, or possibly a sign-on bonus to close the gap?
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你平和地指出：底薪比你基于市场行情和现待遇的期望偏低一点；问底薪有没有浮动空间，或者能不能用签约奖金补上差距。

turns.en: The base band is fixed by level, so I can't move that. A sign-on bonus is possible though — let me check what I can get approved. What would make this a clear yes for you?
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 底薪带是按级别定死的，我动不了。签约奖金倒是有可能，我去看看能批多少。什么条件能让你干脆地答应下来？

turns.en: A sign-on that closes most of the gap would make it work for me. I'd also love to know the review cycle — when would my first performance and salary review be?
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给明确答复：签约奖金补上大部分差距，你就可以定下来；顺便问评估周期——第一次绩效和调薪评估在什么时候。

turns.en: Reviews are annual, but there's a six-month checkpoint for new hires. On start date: the team would love you to start in four weeks. Is that workable?
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 评估是每年一次，但新人有六个月的中期检查。开始时间上，团队希望你四周后入职，你这边可以吗？

turns.en: Four weeks works for me — my notice period is one month, and I'd like to hand over properly. If the sign-on gets approved, I'm ready to sign this week.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你确认四周期限可行（你的交接期正好一个月，你想好好交接）；并表示签约奖金如果批下来，你这周就能签。

turns.en: Perfect. I'll push for the sign-on today and send the updated written offer by tomorrow morning. Anything else you need from me?
turns.name: Daniel
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 太好了。我今天就去争取签约奖金，明天早上之前把更新后的书面 offer 发你。你还需要我提供什么吗？

chunks.term: looking forward to working with you

turns.en: That's everything — I really appreciate it, Daniel. Looking forward to working with you and the team.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你表示没有别的问题了，真诚感谢他，并说期待和他以及团队共事。

scenarios.title: 技术面：深挖你的旗舰项目
scenarios.setting: 技术面，面试官 Priya 看过你的简历，对你主导的“LLM + RAG 生成测试用例、覆盖 85% 测试路径”的质量平台很感兴趣，一路追问细节、取舍和你的个人贡献。你要讲得具体、有数字、不夸大。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: Let's dig into the quality platform on your résumé. In one or two sentences, what problem were you solving?
turns.zh: 我们来深挖一下你简历上的质量平台。用一两句话说，你们当时在解决什么问题？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先给一句话定义：测试用例靠手写，覆盖不全、还慢；你们的平台用大模型加检索生成用例，把核心流程的测试路径覆盖做到了 85%。
turns.en: Our test cases were all written by hand, so coverage was patchy and slow. We built a platform that generates test cases with an LLM grounded by RAG over our own docs and code, and got core-flow path coverage to about eighty-five percent.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: Why RAG? Why not just prompt a big model with the requirements?
turns.zh: 为什么用 RAG？直接拿需求提示大模型不行吗？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你解释取舍：裸提示会编造不存在的接口和规则；检索把生成锚定在真实的代码和规则文档上，幻觉明显减少，生成结果还能引用出处让人审。
turns.en: A raw prompt hallucinates — it invents APIs and business rules that don't exist. Retrieval grounds the generation in our actual code and rule documents, so hallucinations dropped a lot, and every generated case cites its sources, which makes review much easier.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: What was your personal contribution versus the team's?
turns.zh: 这个项目里，哪些是你个人做的，哪些是团队的？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你明确切分：你负责前端架构和生成结果的评审界面（React 18 + Vite），以及评审流程的设计；检索引擎和评估是另外两位后端同事做的。最后落一句：最难的部分是让人愿意信任并使用生成结果。
turns.en: I owned the frontend architecture and the review interface — React 18 with Vite — plus the human review workflow. The retrieval engine and the evaluation harness were built by two backend teammates. Honestly, the hardest part was getting people to trust and actually use the generated cases.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: How did you measure that eighty-five percent? Numbers in interviews are often... optimistic.
turns.zh: 那 85% 是怎么测出来的？面试里的数字经常……比较乐观。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你坦然应对：路径的定义来自状态机穷举的核心流程清单，不是全代码行覆盖；你承认这是团队口径，并说如果重算你愿意把口径文档拿出来对。你强调这个数字不含探索性测试。
turns.en: Fair question. The denominator is an enumerated list of core user flows from our state machines — it's path coverage of those flows, not line coverage of the whole codebase. It's the team's agreed metric; I'm happy to walk through the definition. It doesn't claim anything about exploratory testing.

chunks.zh: 分母（这里指统计口径的总数）

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: If you rebuilt it today, what would you do differently?
turns.zh: 如果今天重做一遍，你会怎么做得不一样？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给两个具体的不同：第一，先做评估集再做生成，不然早期全凭感觉；第二，评审界面一开始就该做批量通过和快捷键，评审速度决定了整个系统的吞吐。
turns.en: Two things. First, I'd build the evaluation set before the generator — early on we tuned by gut feeling. Second, I'd design the review UI for bulk approval and keyboard shortcuts from day one; review speed turned out to be the real throughput limit of the whole system.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Priya
turns.en: That's a thoughtful answer. Let's switch gears to a design problem...
turns.zh: 回答得很扎实。我们换个方向，来看一道设计题……

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你简短地表示没问题，并顺口说设计题你习惯先问澄清问题再动手。
turns.en: Sure — I usually start design problems with a few clarifying questions, if that's okay.

chunks.zh: 如果可以的话（礼貌征询）

scenarios.title: 系统设计面：和面试官一起设计限流系统
scenarios.setting: 系统设计面，面试官 Marcus 让你设计一个给 API 用的分布式限流服务。他更看重你边想边说的过程：一路要澄清规模、讲数据流、谈取舍，遇到他追问时不要慌。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: Let's design a rate limiter service for a public API. Where would you start?
turns.zh: 我们来设计一个给公开 API 用的限流服务。你会从哪儿开始？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先别画图，先问澄清问题：规模多大（请求量、租户数）？限流规则是全局还是按租户/按接口？超限了返回什么？
turns.en: Before drawing anything, let me clarify the scale and the rules. How many requests per second are we designing for, and how many tenants? Are limits global, per tenant, or per endpoint? And when we reject, do we return a 429 with a retry hint?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: Say fifty thousand requests per second, ten thousand tenants, limits per tenant per endpoint. 429 with Retry-After is fine.
turns.zh: 就按每秒五万请求、一万个租户、按租户按接口限流。超限返回 429 带 Retry-After 可以。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你复述确认规模，然后给高层设计：网关层做限流检查，计数放 Redis 用滑动窗口或令牌桶，规则从配置中心下发。强调先说主路径，再谈异常。
turns.en: Got it — fifty thousand a second, per-tenant per-endpoint rules. At a high level: the check sits in the API gateway, counters live in Redis using a sliding window or token bucket, and rules are pushed from a config service. Let me walk through the happy path first, then the failure cases.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: Why Redis? What happens when it goes down — do you fail open or fail closed?
turns.zh: 为什么用 Redis？它挂了怎么办——放行还是拒绝？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你答取舍：Redis 是因为要亚毫秒级的原子计数（Lua 脚本）。挂掉时你的选择是先放行、用本地粗粒度限流兜底，因为限流是为了保护，不该让它单点把 API 拖死；但计费类接口应该反过来。
turns.en: Redis because we need atomic counters with sub-millisecond latency — we'd use a Lua script so the check-and-increment is one step. If Redis goes down, I'd fail open, with a coarse local limit as backup: the limiter exists to protect the API, it shouldn't become the thing that kills it. For billing-sensitive endpoints, I'd flip that choice.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: How accurate does the counting need to be across regions?
turns.zh: 跨区域的计数需要多准？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你反问并给分层答案：如果规则是软性的（防滥用），各区域本地计数加定期汇总就够了，允许小误差；如果必须严格全局配额，就要中心计数，代价是延迟。你建议默认前者。
turns.en: It depends on what the limit protects. For abuse prevention, local counting per region with periodic sync is fine — small overshoot is acceptable. A hard global quota would need central counting, and you pay for it in latency. I'd default to local-first and make strictness a per-rule option.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: One tenant suddenly sends ten times the traffic. What breaks first, and how do you notice?
turns.zh: 有个租户突然发来十倍流量。先坏的是什么？你怎么发现？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你答：先坏的通常不是限流器本身，而是 Redis 的热键和网关的连接数；发现靠三件事——按租户的限流命中率告警、热键监控、以及 429 比例突增的告警。并补一句会给大租户单独分片。
turns.en: What breaks first is usually not the limiter logic — it's hot keys in Redis and connection counts at the gateway. I'd notice through three signals: per-tenant rejection-rate alerts, hot-key monitoring, and a spike alert on the overall 429 ratio. For the largest tenants, I'd shard their counters separately.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marcus
turns.en: Good. We're almost out of time — summarize your design in thirty seconds.
turns.zh: 很好。时间快到了，用三十秒总结一下你的设计。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你收尾总结：网关检查、Redis 原子计数、规则配置化下发；故障时放行加本地兜底；监控盯租户维度的拒绝率。最后问他有没有想深挖的部分。
turns.en: To sum up: checks in the gateway, atomic counters in Redis, rules pushed from config. Fail open with a local fallback if Redis dies, and alert on per-tenant rejection rates so abuse is visible early. Happy to go deeper on any part of that.

scenarios.setting: 最后一轮小组面试，三位面试官。Staff 工程师 Lena 对你简历里“把热更新从 40 秒优化到 8 秒”这一条很感兴趣——而且不打算轻易放过你。
scenarios.title: 终面围攻：面试官咬住一个决定不放

turns.en: You claim hot reload went from forty seconds to eight. Walk me through exactly what was slow. No hand-waving.
turns.name: Lena
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 你说热更新从四十秒优化到了八秒。精确地讲给我听，到底慢在哪儿。不许含糊。

chunks.term: Let me walk you through my thinking.
chunks.zh: 我讲一下我的思考过程

turns.en: Let me walk you through my thinking. Of the forty seconds, a full plug-in scan ate most of it; rebuilding the dependency graph was second. I measured before touching anything.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你按她的要求拆解数字：四十秒里插件全量扫描占大头，其次是依赖图重建；你先定位再动手，讲清思路的顺序。

turns.en: Anyone can say 'we added caching'. What exactly did you cache, and what broke because of it?
turns.name: Lena
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 谁都会说“我们加了缓存”。你到底缓存了什么？又因为缓存坏过什么？

chunks.term: I can elaborate on ... if that's useful.
chunks.zh: 如果需要，我可以展开讲……

turns.en: We cached module resolution results keyed by file fingerprint. What broke: a stale read in week two, when an edited dependency did not invalidate. I fixed it with a reverse dependency index. I can elaborate on the invalidation if that's useful.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给出细节并主动交代代价：缓存的是模块解析结果，键是文件指纹；代价是上线第二周出现过一次脏读——改了被依赖文件却没失效，你用依赖反向索引补上了。

turns.en: Why not just upgrade the bundler version instead of all this surgery?
turns.name: Lena
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 为什么不直接升级打包工具版本，非要做这么多手术？

chunks.term: Just to make sure I understood...

turns.en: Just to make sure I understood: why not take the upgrade path? Because the plug-in ecosystem pinned the version; upgrading would have broken a dozen internal plug-ins at once. Surgery was the smaller risk.
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先确认自己理解了她的问题再回答：她问的是为什么不用现成升级路径——因为当时插件生态锁死了版本，升级会同时打断十几个内部插件，风险比手术大。

turns.en: How do you know the eight seconds wasn't mostly the new CI machines you got that quarter?
turns.name: Lena
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 你怎么知道那八秒不主要是你们那季度换了新 CI 机器的功劳？

chunks.term: Am I on the right track?

turns.en: Same machine, same repo, fifty runs before and after, median compared. The new hardware alone was worth under a second — we measured it separately. Am I on the right track for what you wanted?
turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你给出对照证据并自查轨道：同一台机器、同一仓库、改动前后各跑五十次取中位数，机器红利单独测过、只占不到一秒；你确认一下自己答得对不对路。

turns.en: That's the first answer today with its own control group. Good. Let's move to the system design part.
turns.name: Lena
turns.speaker: them
turns.zh: 这是今天第一个自带对照组的回答。不错。我们进入系统设计环节。
